extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in higher education, educational psychology, and teacher education (especially those studying mathematics identity and preservice teacher development)
extracted.subtask_description: A preregistered empirical study measuring and comparing preservice mathematics teachers' and major mathematics students' identities in mathematics using constructs of task value, sense of belonging, and identification, including participants' beliefs about how the other group perceives these constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task value (intrinsic, attainment/personal importance, utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures 'What is mathematics for me?' reflecting the personal appreciation of mathematics via task value derived from Eccles & Wigfield's (1995) expectancy value theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task value differentiates how learning material is interesting (intrinsic value), important (attainment/personal importance), and useful (utility value). In this study participants indicate their perceived task value of studying academic mathematics along these subdimensions; preservice teachers also rate what they believe major mathematics students perceive on the same subdimensions, and vice versa for major students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of belonging in academic mathematics (membership, acceptance, desire to fade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures 'What am I in mathematics?' capturing how a student perceives to fit into the discipline of mathematics via sense of belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sense of belonging includes the sub facets membership, acceptance, and desire to fade, which are closely linked (Good et al., 2012). Participants report their sense of belonging in academic mathematics on these facets; preservice teachers and major students also provide ratings of what they believe the other group perceives on these facets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as a mathematics student (academic and non-academic settings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants indicate their identification as a mathematics student in an academic setting and separately in a non-academic setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures contextualized self-identification (how much one identifies as a mathematics student depending on setting) and complements task value and sense of belonging measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-perceptions by preservice teachers about major students' task value and belonging
rubrics_metrics.description: Preservice teachers rate what task value (intrinsic, personal importance, utility) and sense of belonging (membership, acceptance, desire to fade) they believe major mathematics students perceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ratings capture preservice teachers' beliefs about how fostered major students' identities in mathematics are, serving as a perceived-other perspective to compare against majors' self-reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-perceptions by major mathematics students about preservice teachers' task value and belonging
rubrics_metrics.description: Major mathematics students rate what task value (intrinsic, personal importance, utility) and sense of belonging (membership, acceptance, desire to fade) they believe preservice teachers perceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ratings capture majors' beliefs about preservice teachers' identities in mathematics, enabling comparison between self-perceptions and outsiders' perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative hypotheses about fostered identity (group differences and perceived differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research questions/hypotheses that test whether preservice teachers indicate a less fostered identity in mathematics than major mathematics students, whether preservice teachers believe they have a less fostered identity than majors believe, and whether majors believe preservice teachers have a less fostered identity than majors report for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study compares self-reports and cross-group meta-perceptions to determine discrepancies between groups and between self- and other-perceptions; these comparative contrasts are central to the study's evaluation of identity fosteredness across program types (teacher education vs mathematics major).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-construct framework: 'What is mathematics for me?' vs 'What am I in mathematics?'
rubrics_metrics.description: An overarching conceptual rubric using two different questions to frame identity: (1) personal appreciation (task value) and (2) perceived fit (sense of belonging).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study applies constructs that reflect these two questions to comprehensively assess students' identity in mathematics; these constructs guide instrument selection and interpretation of results.
